edition: Graduale Romanum (Solesmes, 1961), Kyriale I · Tempore Paschali (Lux et origo)
method: Visually inspected original printed Kyriale facsimile pages 4*, 5*, 6*, and 7* at PDF page positions 6–9 (one-based), distinguishing the surrounding Asperges and Ite missa est music from Mass I Ordinary movements.

Compared identifiable printed Latin clause boundaries, printed starts/ends, explicit Kyrie repeat markers, Sanctus/Benedictus continuity and Agnus endings to the four unmodified local GregoBase GABC transcriptions.
Source GABC note-bearing groups are inventory counts from a deterministic parser. They are NOT a count of manually verified printed notes or agreement in pitch.

No claim of exhaustive printed absolute pitch, neume shape, episemata, rhythmic signs, accidentals, custos, individual syllable underlay or publisher/editorial approval. No unapproved musical source was rewritten.

sourceWitnesses.observed: Bottom of page: Mass I Kyrie begins; earlier chant on the page is Asperges me, not Kyrie I
Kyrie I concludes at top and Gloria I begins; Gloria continues onto page 6*
Gloria I concludes with Amen; Sanctus I starts, including Benedictus qui venit
Sanctus I completes Benedictus and final Hosanna; complete three-invocation Agnus I follows; dismissal chants beneath Agnus are separate music

scoreSurveys.title: Kyrie I · Lux et origo
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Four notated sections: Kyrie iij., Christe iij., Kyrie ij., terminal Kyrie once (3+3+2+1 invocations)
observations: Kyrie heading and first Kyrie/Christe section visibly begin at bottom of p.4*
Christe completes at top of p.5*, followed by Kyrie ij. and distinct terminal Kyrie
Do not flatten the last Kyrie into a repeat of the opening melody

scoreSurveys.title: Gloria I
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Continuous Gloria from Gloria in excelsis Deo to concluding Amen
observations: Opening Gloria is printed beneath Kyrie on p.5*
The line beginning Qui tollis peccata mundi crosses the printed 5*→6* page boundary
Gloria ends at Amen on p.6*, before the separately headed Sanctus

scoreSurveys.title: Sanctus I with Benedictus
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Sanctus ×3, Pleni sunt caeli, Hosanna, Benedictus qui venit, final Hosanna
observations: Sanctus starts on p.6* after Gloria Amen; the Benedictus phrase begins before the page break
In nomine Domini and the final Hosanna continue on p.7*
Both Hosanna passages must remain in one Sanctus–Benedictus score and canonical Mass card

scoreSurveys.title: Agnus Dei I
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Three complete invocations: miserere nobis twice; third ends dona nobis pacem
observations: Agnus I begins on p.7* below the last Hosanna of Sanctus I
All three Agnus invocations and the final dona nobis pacem are on p.7*
The separate Ite missa est/Deo gratias lines beneath do not belong to Agnus I; this Ordinary score is not a Requiem variant
